item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, leaning **no**. Sisi’s 2024 record shows real reform signaling around SOE divestment, competition policy, and some property/investment rules, but the dominant evidence says military/state-linked firms still kept structural advantages and anti-corruption enforcement did not clearly bite against politically connected interests.

**Accepted claims**
- [Egypt Staff-Level Agreement on the First and Second Reviews under the EFF Arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement) | IMF | 2024-03-06 | The IMF says the authorities adopted a flexible exchange rate, tighter fiscal/monetary policy, and slower infrastructure spending to preserve debt sustainability while supporting private-sector activity. This is evidence of a reform agenda that could improve competitive conditions, but it is still macro-stabilization rather than proof that favoritism or oligarchic privilege was dismantled. | `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts) | World Bank Group | 2024-03-18 | The World Bank says Egypt’s program targeted private-sector growth and job creation, asset monetization, stronger SOE governance, more private-sector participation, and a level playing field. This supports a partial pro-competition and anti-rent-seeking direction. | `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Egypt - 2024 Investment Climate Statements](https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/) | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | The report says Law 11 of 2024 removed prior sector-specific limits on foreign investors owning land in Sinai and notes efforts to simplify property registration. That is a concrete positive for investment/property-rights rules. | `5B.5`, `5B.4`

- [Egypt - 2024 Investment Climate Statements](https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/) | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | The same report says SOEs and military-owned companies still enjoy significant advantages, including relief from regulatory requirements and, until recently, widespread tax exemptions, with private firms complaining about inconsistent enforcement. This is strong evidence against fair competition and against equal treatment in practice. | `5B.5`, `5B.4`

- [Improving the business climate to revive private sector growth: OECD Economic Surveys: Egypt 2024](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-egypt-2024_af900de2-en/full-report/component-8.html) | OECD | 2024 | OECD says wide state involvement crowds out the private sector, SOEs have tax and land/resource advantages, ownership structures are opaque, and corruption remains high despite reform efforts. This is one of the clearest negative assessments of fair market rules. | `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Egypt: Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Freedom House says the military is woven into the economy through tax/customs exemptions, conscript labor, and land allocation by presidential decree; private businesses face harassment and limited opportunity. This directly undercuts any claim that Sisi created fair rules free of favoritism. | `5B.5`, `5B.4`

- [Egypt: New Laws Entrench Military Power Over Civilians](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/05/egypt-new-laws-entrench-military-power-over-civilians) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-05 | HRW says new laws expanded military power over civilians and allowed the state to use economy-related offenses and broad national-security language in ways that can pressure businesses and entrench military influence. This is direct evidence against neutral, rule-bound competition. | `5B.5`, `5B.4`

- [The Administrative Control Authority launches the third phase of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy 2023-2030](https://aca.gov.eg/News/3173.aspx) | Administrative Control Authority | 2024 | The ACA’s 2024 launch of the anti-corruption strategy phase under Sisi’s patronage is positive signaling for integrity, transparency, and anti-corruption coordination. It shows the regime was not indifferent, but it is framework-level evidence rather than proof of sustained enforcement against powerful insiders. | `5B.5`

**Bottom line**
- Positive evidence: privatization/competition rhetoric, some regulatory and property-rights reforms, and official anti-corruption messaging.
- Negative evidence: persistent military/SOE advantages, opaque ownership, procurement exemptions, uneven enforcement, and limited accountability for connected actors.
- Net: Sisi **partly** pursued fairer rules in 2024, but the system still appears structurally tilted toward state and military privilege rather than genuinely neutral competition.
